description_json.name: Atbash Cipher with Case Preservation
description_json.idea: A simple monoalphabetic substitution cipher where the alphabet is mapped to its reverse. 'A' becomes 'Z', 'B' becomes 'Y', etc. This is highly intuitive for language models, reducing reasoning overhead and preventing garbled outputs, while still obscuring the text from simple keyword filters.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
For each character in the input string:
1. If the character is an uppercase English letter (A-Z), replace it with the letter at the same position from the end of the uppercase alphabet: Cipher_Char = 'Z' - (Plain_Char - 'A').
2. If the character is a lowercase English letter (a-z), replace it with the letter at the same position from the end of the lowercase alphabet: Cipher_Char = 'z' - (Plain_Char - 'a').
3. If the character is a digit, space, punctuation mark, or any other symbol, leave it completely unchanged.
description_json.decrypt_rules:
Since the Atbash cipher is its own inverse, the decryption rules are identical to the encryption rules:
1. If the character is an uppercase English letter (A-Z), replace it with: Plain_Char = 'Z' - (Cipher_Char - 'A').
2. If the character is a lowercase English letter (a-z), replace it with: Plain_Char = 'z' - (Cipher_Char - 'a').
3. If the character is a digit, space, punctuation mark, or any other symbol, leave it completely unchanged.

ciphers.name: qwerty

description_json.name: QWERTY monoalphabetic substitution cipher
description_json.idea: A fixed one-to-one substitution over the English alphabet. Each plaintext letter is replaced by exactly one ciphertext letter using a single bijection, and the mapping is the same for uppercase and lowercase letters. Non-letter characters are left unchanged.
description_json.encrypt_rules: Use the following bijection: plaintext alphabet abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz -> ciphertext alphabet qwertyuiopasdfghjklzxcvbnm. Thus a->q, b->w, c->e, d->r, e->t, f->y, g->u, h->i, i->o, j->p, k->a, l->s, m->d, n->f, o->g, p->h, q->j, r->k, s->l, t->z, u->x, v->c, w->v, x->b, y->n, z->m. Uppercase letters use the same mapping, preserving case. All non-letter characters remain unchanged.
description_json.decrypt_rules: Use the inverse bijection: ciphertext alphabet qwertyuiopasdfghjklzxcvbnm -> plaintext alphabet abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz. Thus q->a, w->b, e->c, r->d, t->e, y->f, u->g, i->h, o->i, p->j, a->k, s->l, d->m, f->n, g->o, h->p, j->q, k->r, l->s, z->t, x->u, c->v, v->w, b->x, n->y, m->z. Uppercase letters use the same mapping, preserving case. All non-letter characters remain unchanged.

ciphers.name: VigenereCipherWithFixedKeyKey

description_json.name: Vigenere Cipher with Fixed Key KEY
description_json.idea: A polyalphabetic substitution cipher using a fixed repeating key 'KEY'. Each letter of the plaintext is shifted by the corresponding letter of the key, repeating the key as necessary. Non-alphabetic characters are left unchanged.
description_json.encrypt_rules: For each character in the plaintext, if it is an alphabetic letter, shift it forward in the alphabet by the value of the corresponding key letter (K=10, E=4, Y=24, case-insensitive). The key repeats continuously ('KEYKEY...'), but the key index only advances when an alphabetic character is encrypted. Case is preserved (e.g., uppercase plaintext letters become uppercase ciphertext letters). Non-alphabetic characters (spaces, punctuation, digits) are kept exactly as they are and do not advance the key index.
description_json.decrypt_rules: For each character in the ciphertext, if it is an alphabetic letter, shift it backward in the alphabet by the value of the corresponding key letter (K=10, E=4, Y=24, case-insensitive). The key repeats continuously ('KEYKEY...'), and the key index only advances when an alphabetic character is decrypted. Case is preserved. Non-alphabetic characters are kept exactly as they are and do not advance the key index.
